title: Walk a tuple
description:
A `std::tuple` holds values of different types, so an ordinary loop cannot visit them: the loop variable would need a different type each time round. The answer is to expand a **pack of indices** at compile time.

Write:

- `template <typename... Ts> std::string tupleText(const std::tuple<Ts...>& t)`: the elements written out, separated by `", "` and wrapped in brackets, for example `"(1, two, 3.5)"`. An empty tuple gives `"()"`.
- `template <typename... Ts, typename F> void forEach(const std::tuple<Ts...>& t, F function)`: calls `function` on every element in order.

`std::apply(callable, tuple)` calls `callable` with the tuple's elements as separate arguments, which hands you a pack to fold over. (The lower-level tool is `std::index_sequence`; either is fine.)
